title: Gemini gets a huge shopping upgrade right before Black Friday
excerpt: Gemini's new shopping overlay can help you to buy better and smarter, and above all, cheaper.
content_html:
Published Nov 25, 2026, 6:13 AM EST

Mark has been covering smart devices for the better part of a decade now. He wrote over a thousand articles for Digital Trends and worked as an editor there, before moving to Android Police in 2025.

He's written about everything from budget phones to flagship phones, e-readers, smartwatches, fitness trackers, and anything else that might connect to a smartphone in some way. 

Starting his mobile tech career with accessory seller Mobile Fun, he's unusually obsessed with stuff that clips onto or connects to phones, and he loves it when a new accessory lands on his desk.

He worked for Digital Trends from 2017 to 2025.

Google Gemini can now use its floating overlay to compare shopping prices, and offer insights on warranty and return terms, removing a large admin task from your big purchases.

As part of a larger Gemini update rolling out now, Google's AI can help you choose whether to buy a particular product, and whether you'd be better off buying it from another store, based on warranty terms, returns policy, and other details.

Leaving the dopamine rush to you alone

Online shopping can be simple. You can buy a product from one place, and never stop to wonder if you could get it cheaper elsewhere, or with better returns or warranty. It only takes one time for you to realize you could be shopping smarter for you to take it seriously.

And while that can save you money, it's a time-sink instead. Researching different shops, comparing prices, reading small print and reviews — ugh! It's easier when someone else does it for you.

Gemini is now hoping you'll let it do the hard work instead, as Google is rolling out the ability for it to help you shop and do your research.

Once the update hits your phone, opening Gemini's floating overlay while a shopping app or website is open will let it help out.

It'll immediately offer you three options to get started: "Help me pick", "Compare prices", and "Check warranty and returns". The three are as straightforward as they sound, and will follow up with any relevant information that might be helpful for you. It'll be able to compare each of the details against other prominent retailers, and offer advice based on that information.

It's not hard to see how this might be immediately helpful right before Black Friday hits the US. One of the biggest problems on Black Friday is feeling pressured to grab a deal while it's there. Ticking timers are the enemy of considered purchases, and having a tool like Gemini that can quickly look up other options is very valuable.

I don't have this update yet, which may be more because I'm in the UK rather than the US. But as generally positive as I am about AI filling areas like this, I still have some qualms. For one, AI is often wrong. Hallucinations and bad information are simply built into AI as it is right now, and there's no getting around the fact it may just lie to you. So it's always in your best interests to check everything it tells you.

Second, there's a strong "use it or lose it" element here. Sure, comparing prices and returns procedures isn't the biggest skill in the world, but the process of doing it yourself is still valuable, so you may want to think twice about offboarding all your effort to a bot.

Still, it's generally no worse than using a third-party website for this sort of research, so personally, I'll be sure to use this once it's available.

This update is currently rolling out, so if you don't have it yet, just wait and see if it turns up.
